name: pypi
description: PyPI (Python Package Index): look up Python packages and specific versions, read release, update and new-package RSS feeds, see top projects by size and index-wide totals, and fetch the GitHub repo stats and issues that PyPI project pages show.

commands.name: get-package
commands.summary: Get a package's PyPI page for its latest version: name and version, summary, pip install command, project links and metadata sidebar, and README text.

params.name: name
params.description: Package name as it appears on PyPI, e.g. requests

commands.name: get-package-version
commands.summary: Get the PyPI page for one specific version of a package: header, summary, pinned pip command, metadata sidebar and the README as it was at that release.

commands.name: list-package-releases
commands.summary: List a package's recent releases (version, link, publish date) from its releases RSS feed.

commands.name: list-latest-updates
commands.summary: List the newest releases uploaded across all of PyPI (package + version, link, date) from the site-wide updates RSS feed.

commands.name: list-newest-packages
commands.summary: List projects newly created on PyPI (name, link, summary, date) from the newest-packages RSS feed.

commands.name: list-top-projects-by-size
commands.summary: List the top 100 PyPI projects ranked by the total size of their release files. The first row is the total for all of PyPI.

commands.name: get-index-totals
commands.summary: Get PyPI-wide totals shown on the homepage (number of projects, releases, files, users).

commands.name: get-github-repo
commands.summary: Get the GitHub statistics PyPI shows for a project's source repo (stars, forks, open issues, description, last push), from the GitHub API.

params.name: owner
params.description: GitHub user or organization that owns the repo (from the package's Source link), e.g. psf

commands.name: search-github-issues
commands.summary: Search GitHub issues and PRs with a GitHub query, e.g. the open issues of a package's repo, via the GitHub search API (the same call PyPI uses to show open-issue counts).

params.name: q
params.description: GitHub issue search query, e.g. 'repo:psf/requests type:issue state:open'

notes: Keyword search (/search/) is blocked by robots.txt and the JSON API (/pypi/{name}/json) is disallowed, so there is no search command. To find a package, use its exact name with get-package, or browse list-newest-packages / list-latest-updates.

PyPI sometimes answers HTML pages with a bot 'Client Challenge' page instead of content. This happened for /project/httpx/0.27.0/ and /user/{name}/ profile pages. If get-package or get-package-version returns empty fields, retry later or use the RSS commands.
User profile pages and /rss/user/{name}/packages.xml were not usable (challenge page / 404), so there is no user command.
list-package-releases uses the RSS feed, which only carries the most recent releases. Use get-package-version for a specific older version.

get-github-repo and search-github-issues call api.github.com directly. Unauthenticated requests are rate-limited (about 60 per hour for the REST API and 10 per minute for search). Get owner/repo from the 'Source' link in the get-package sidebar.
The first row of list-top-projects-by-size is the 'All of PyPI' total, not a project.
